purpose: Close ASVS V4.2.5, and correct a record that had never been assessed against its own requirement. The previous decision's note described SSRF - a partner pointing a webhook at an internal service or a metadata endpoint - and V4.2.5 does not ask that. It asks that an application which builds and sends requests avoid creating URIs or header fields too long for the receiving component to accept, because an over-length request line or header field is answered with 414 or 431 every time and becomes a denial of service. The SSRF property is real and was closed separately in #4805 and #4816; borrowing it as this requirement's evidence meant V4.2.5 was never assessed at all.
requiredInvariants: The limits are enforced at the single place every outbound request passes, not where the value happens to be stored. A ceiling applied at registration is bypassed by any caller that builds a request from something else, and the value here is stored by an endpoint whose inline body type no validation class acts on.

Both limits are measured in bytes. A server counts octets and one Cyrillic character is two of them; on this platform that is the ordinary case rather than a corner one, and a character count would pass a value twice the size the server actually sees.

The header check runs ahead of the redirect loop. The header set does not change between hops, so a refusal must precede the first connection rather than follow a request that already went out and came back with a 302.

The ceilings are taken from the smallest documented limits among the servers a webhook is likely to reach, not from a preference of this application: nginx defaults to an 8 KiB request line and 8 KiB header buffers, so 2 KiB of URI and 4 KiB per header value inside an 8 KiB total stays acceptable to all of them.
The field name and separators are counted against the total, because that is what the server counts against its buffer.

A size refusal returns its own reason and never reaches the transport, so it stays distinguishable from a request that was attempted and failed. That distinction is the same one the SSRF cases in this file rely on.
The address rules from #4816 are not touched, weakened or reordered. This adds a size property beside them; where a request goes is decided exactly as before.
No production, REG.RU, DNS, database or credential mutation. No migration, no new dependency. New mandatory cost: 0 RUB.
acceptance: Five mutations, each caught: removing the URI ceiling fails 3, removing the header check fails 3, measuring the URI in characters fails 1, dropping the total-size check fails 1, measuring header values in characters fails 1.

That last one is recorded because it originally failed NOTHING. The byte-measurement case existed for the URI and not for headers, so the property the code comment claimed was unasserted, and the mutation survived a full green run. The case was added and the mutation now fails - the same defect this programme keeps finding, this time in a test written in the same hour.

V4.2.5 moves FAIL to PASS against origin/main measured directly: PASS 119 to 120, FAIL 100 to 99, with no other verdict moved. Three negative mutations each revoke the condition they target at the matrix level.
